messages:
alex_support: FYI customer reported a large delta between dashboard token counts and invoice for streaming calls. They say streaming sessions with client-initiated pause/resume look 20-30% higher on the invoice. Request ID: r-7f9.

alex_support: Customer pasted an SSE snippet and short transcript — they do a pause (client closes connection) then reconnect within 3s. They include this server SSE sequence: 

alex_support: ```
event: chunk
data: {\"seq\":1, \"tokens\":120}

event: chunk
data: {\"seq\":2, \"tokens\":80}

event: final
data: {\"total_tokens\":200}

# client disconnects (HTTP close) then reconnects
event: chunk
data: {\"seq\":3, \"tokens\":30}

event: final
data: {\"total_tokens\":230}
```

alex_support: Customer thinks the second final caused double-counting (dashboard shows 230, invoice charged as if both finals counted = 430 tokens).

morgan_repro: Can confirm we saw similar repro in internal test last week when testing pause/resume. Need request_id and connection ids from logs — alex do you have raw logs?

alex_support: Pasted trace lines from frontdoor for r-7f9: 

alex_support: ```
[2026-03-04T14:12:01Z] FRONTDOOR conn=s-112 req=r-7f9 event=chunk seq=1 tokens=120
[2026-03-04T14:12:03Z] FRONTDOOR conn=s-112 req=r-7f9 event=chunk seq=2 tokens=80
[2026-03-04T14:12:05Z] FRONTDOOR conn=s-112 req=r-7f9 event=final total=200
[2026-03-04T14:12:06Z] FRONTDOOR conn=s-112 req=r-7f9 event=close reason=client_pause
[2026-03-04T14:12:08Z] FRONTDOOR conn=s-113 req=r-7f9 event=chunk seq=3 tokens=30
[2026-03-04T14:12:09Z] FRONTDOOR conn=s-113 req=r-7f9 event=final total=230
```

jamie_billing: Billing notes: our metering pipeline records a finalize event and adds tokens to invoice when we see a FINAL_MARKER from metering-service. If a second FINAL_MARKER arrives with a different session id but same request_id and we don't dedupe on session, both get billed.

li_engineering: Quick hypothesis: frontdoor emits final per connection (conn/session) and metering currently dedupes by request_id only for short TTL, but reconnects reuse request_id (customer provided same request_id on reconnect) so we see two distinct final events scoped to different session ids. We need dedupe to include session id or ensure reconnects don't reuse request_id.

morgan_repro: Repro steps I used locally (worked):

morgan_repro: 1) Open SSE stream with Authorization header for model/generate.
morgan_repro: 2) Let server stream two chunks and a final.
morgan_repro: 3) Close the TCP connection (client-side pause).
morgan_repro: 4) Reopen a new SSE connection, re-send the same request_id header, receive additional chunk + final.

morgan_repro: Example curl to repro: ```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TEST\" -H \"X-Request-ID: r-repro\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?model=gpt-mini
# close then reopen with same X-Request-ID
```

li_engineering: I've reproduced in staging. Logs show two finalize events with different conn ids. Metering currently logs: 

li_engineering: ```
[METERING] finalize request_id=r-repro session=s-201 tokens=200
[METERING] finalize request_id=r-repro session=s-202 tokens=30
```

li_engineering: Root cause: dedupe key too coarse — should include session id or a generation sequence id. Two options: (A) update metering dedupe key to request_id+session_id (quick), (B) change frontdoor to preserve a single final per request_id across reconnects (more invasive).

jamie_billing: For the customer impact: we should proactively issue a credit for the duplicate finals while we roll the quick fix. Can you produce an affected-invoices list for r-7f9 and the last 30 days?

alex_support: I'll ask the customer for permission to search their invoices and attach a sample. Also collecting other request_ids from them.

morgan_repro: Quick mitigation patch is small (metering service) — add session id into dedupe key and backfill a reconciliation job that collapses duplicates from same request_id within 10s window. I'll open a PR and staging job.

li_engineering: Note: need to be careful with long-polling clients that intentionally resume – TTL window choice matters. We'll run integration tests against streaming scenarios (client pause, network flap, reconnect reuse request_id).

jamie_billing: Once we have the list, I'll prepare an invoice adjustment template and mark as high-priority. Also flag finance to avoid auto collections for affected accounts for 7 days.

alex_support: Customer is grateful and asked for expected ETA. Morgan do you have ETA on staging->prod?

morgan_repro: PR today, staging test tomorrow, deploy canary in 48h if tests pass. Will DM if anything blocks. :white_check_mark:

jamie_billing: Thanks team. Tagging infra bot to run one-off reconciliation for r-7f9 so we can calculate exact credit amount: @infra_bot run-reconcile --request r-7f9

infra_bot: acknowledged: queued job 78621 to scan metering logs for request_id=r-7f9 and produce candidate duplicate finals.

li_engineering: Adding follow-up: we'll add a metric for duplicate-final rate per hour so we can detect regressions.

alex_support: I'll update the customer with the plan and ETA. If they authorize, I'll attach their invoice sample here.

jamie_billing: Keep me posted, please include invoice ids in this thread so we can apply credits quickly. :thumbsup:

alex_support: will do. cc @incidents if this starts affecting multiple customers.

morgan_repro: saving repro steps to docs/streaming/reconnect-metering.md after the PR.

li_engineering: ok locking — will follow up with a postmortem link after rollout. :thinking:
